articles.title: A Miniaturized Electrostatic Field Sensor Based on MOS Depletion-Layer Capacitance Modulation
Molecular profiling of repeated self-sampled blood reveals dynamic immune phenotypes in young adults
articles.abstract: Abstract Although population-based studies of circulating blood proteins have provided profound insight into human biology, transient changes to time-dependent exposures often remain elusive. Here, we perform a longitudinal dried blood spot (DBS) self-sampling study in 808 young adults (aged 24–27, 64% females) from the Swedish Barn [Children], Allergy, Milieu, Stockholm Epidemiology cohort. In total, we collected ~2400 samples from 2020 to 2022. Each sample was profiled for SARS-CoV-2 serological, anti-interferon autoantibodies (AAbs), and 365 inflammation-related proteins. We subsequently linked these samples to registry-confirmed infection and vaccination exposures, physiological traits, genetic variation, and blood counts. We show that data-driven seroclustering captures the response to both infection and vaccination exposures, while stable AAbs against interferon receptors IFNAR1 and IFNGR2 associate with the duration of self-reported COVID-19 symptoms. Genome-wide mapping reveals 664 protein quantitative trait loci (pQTL) across 65 proteins, with cis -pQTLs associated proteins showing greater longitudinal stability. Paired pre- and post-exposure samples indicate temporal changes in protein levels after infection (LAP3) and vaccination (TIMP3). This multi-molecular epidemiological profiling of self-sampled blood captures dynamic immune trajectories and shorter-term variability in a population of young adults.

articles.title: Theoretical frameworks for credit assignment via behavioral timescale synaptic plasticity
articles.abstract: Abstract Behavioral Timescale Synaptic Plasticity (BTSP) is a form of plasticity which drives place field formation in hippocampal pyramidal neurons. Unlike traditional learning rules, BTSP learns pre-post correlations on timescales of seconds and rapidly changes single-unit activity in only a few trials. To study how BTSP-like learning can be integrated into network models, we propose a generalized theoretical framework, gBTSP, which we apply to unsupervised and supervised tasks in feedforward and recurrent networks. We show that unsupervised gBTSP learns place field maps in the feedforward case and attractor memories in the recurrent case. For supervised learning, we derive how plateau events can reduce task error, enabling gBTSP to solve trajectory matching and delayed non-match-to-sample tasks. Finally, we find that the speed of credit assignment via gBTSP is limited by network depth or CA3-like recurrence, suggesting that additional mechanisms are necessary to account for BTSP-driven few-shot learning in naturalistic settings.

articles.title: Chirality-locked low-dimensional bound states in the continuum lasers
articles.abstract: Abstract Bound states in the continuum (BICs) support high-quality-factor resonances embedded in extended spectra, and their radiation properties can be tailored through perturbative symmetry breaking and chiral engineering. However, because BICs are intrinsically delocalized states of infinite periodic structures, they typically require large spatial footprints. Achieving localized BIC modes while preserving radiation suppression and topological singularities, and simultaneously enabling chiral responses, remains a challenge. Here, we experimentally realize low-threshold BIC lasers localized at one-dimensional interfaces and zero-dimensional junctions by interfacing domains with identical bulk BIC characteristics but opposite chirality. The resulting interfaces and junctions host spatially localized states that exhibit optical spin–momentum-locked emission governed by the assigned chirality, while retaining intrinsic BIC properties, including narrow far-field divergence and pump-selective lasing localization. In addition, polarization singularities confirm the topological nature of these low-dimensional BICs, particularly the well-defined topological charge of the zero-dimensional junction mode. Coupling two zero-dimensional BICs further gives rise to bonding and antibonding supermodes, enabling non-Hermitian, chirality-locked behaviors. These results establish a route to compact, high-quality-factor photonic states with engineered chirality through dimensional reduction of BICs, without relying on defect confinement or band inversion.

articles.title: Photocatalytic radical hydrogenation of unactivated alkenes via an intermolecular hydrogen-atom-transfer relay
Emergent mesoscale nanoparticle patterns from a non-equilibrium liquid lens
A subspecialty diagnostic system powered by self-supervised learning for cervical histopathology
Taming crystallization to achieve superior soft magnetic performance via fine nanocrystallines
Chemogenetic dissection of the H2O2–salicylic acid feedback loop in PTI and ETI evolutionary conservation
Phenotypic variation in Drosophila complex traits is influenced more by genotype and environmental interactions than by mitonuclear coevolutionary history
Sensory cortical disinhibition underlies long-term fear memory in humans
articles.abstract: Abstract How transient threats turn into persistent, long-term fear memories is a fundamental problem in neuroscience, yet the underlying mechanisms remain elusive. Early sensory cortex, traditionally viewed as a passive feature analyzer, is increasingly recognized as an active participant in fear processing. Combining high-definition α-frequency transcranial alternating current stimulation (HD α-tACS) with simultaneous EEG-fMRI (electroencephalography-functional magnetic resonance imaging) and transformer-based neural decoding, we tracked fear memory development across formation, consolidation, and long-term retention (assessed at 15 min, 24 h, and 7 days after fear conditioning). Spatiotemporal memory traces were identified at all three assessments, beginning at an early sensory stage (40–60 ms post-stimulus) and distributed across visual cortex and limbic regions. Conditioning potentiated occipital α-oscillation desynchronization, a marker of visual cortical disinhibition, which subsequently predicted the strength of long-term memory traces. Critically, targeted α-tACS over early visual cortex induced early visual cortical (V1/V2) inhibition, abolished conditioning-potentiated α desynchronization, and selectively disrupted fear-memory consolidation and retention while leaving initial acquisition intact. These findings establish sensory cortical disinhibition as a necessary mechanism for long-term fear memory in humans and identify early sensory cortex as crucial node for intervention of persistent maladaptive fear.

articles.title: Enhancer-driven gene regulatory network of human forebrain development provides insights into autism
Tuning methanol-CO selectivity in CO2 hydrogenation by Ga coordination engineering in ZnGa2O4
Glutamine binding and sodium coordination reveal the transport mechanism of y⁺LAT1/CD98hc
Multi-ancestry genetic analysis reveals 29 novel rheumatoid arthritis loci, effector genes and drug repurposing opportunities
articles.abstract: Abstract Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a complex autoimmune disease with a substantial heritable component. We perform multi-ancestry genome-wide association meta-analyses of 351,498 individuals (comprising 39,600 RA cases and 311,898 controls) by integrating published and new datasets. This analysis identifies 29 novel RA susceptibility loci and systematically classifies association signals as population-specific, population-dominant, or population-shared between East Asian and European populations. Bayesian fine-mapping and functional annotation prioritize putative causal variants, highlighting 67 variants with posterior inclusion probability>0.1 in novel loci, including an SLC27A6 missense variant (rs137898880) and a STIM1 3′ UTR variant (rs3750996). Our gene-prioritization framework combining genetic and biological evidence identifies 203 high-confidence effector genes, 16 of which reside in novel loci (e.g., IFI16 , AIM2 , RGS1 , ITPKB , CD80 , RHOH , NFKB1 , SIK3 , and CCND2 ). Colocalization analysis leveraging tissue-specific eQTL datasets provides mechanistic insights by implicating shared causal variants underlying RA association signals. Notably, the transcription factor gene RUNX3 at a novel locus shows evidence of cis -regulation in immune cells, and RUNX3-binding sites are enriched for variants explaining excess RA heritability, suggesting a potential role for RUNX3 as a trans -regulatory mediator of RA risk at distal RA loci. Finally, exploratory gene-drug interaction networks weighted by RA association strength highlight population-informed therapeutic opportunities and drug-repurposing targets driven largely by novel loci.

articles.title: Global patterns of radial growth-structural heterogeneity relationships in forests
DPI-score: a deep learning-based metric for assessing protein-protein interfaces in cryoEM derived assemblies
articles.abstract: Abstract Advances in cryoEM have led to a surge in high-resolution structures; however, model building and refinement at resolutions ( > = 3 Å) and in regions with variable local resolution remain challenging, making validation essential. CryoEM derived assemblies often contain extensive protein-protein interfaces, however, most existing validation metrics focus on density fit or overall geometry without directly assessing interface quality. To address this, we present DPI-Score, a deep learning-based metric for assessing protein-protein interfaces in cryoEM derived complexes. The method uses only raw structural coordinates of interface atoms, without requiring engineered features, and achieves 87.53% validation accuracy. DPI-Score was applied to 29,120 interfaces from 6,011 fitted entries with resolutions worse than 3 Å in the Electron Microscopy Data Bank. Here, we show that DPI-Score provides complementary information to existing validation metrics and can identify interface errors in modelled assemblies that are not detected by density-based scores alone.

articles.title: Kinetic balancing for near-equilibrium growth of defect-suppressed lead bromide perovskite single crystals
Field-angle-resolved heat transport in UTe2: determination of nodal positions in the superconducting order parameter
articles.abstract: Abstract One of the recurring hurdles in studying unconventional superconductivity is the challenge of efficiently and conclusively identifying the symmetry of the superconducting order parameter in a new material. Uranium ditelluride (UTe 2 ) exhibits an unprecedented number of superconducting phases, and none of them has had its symmetry conclusively identified so far. Here we report results of an extensive study of the thermal conductivity of UTe 2 in the superconducting state as a function of the angle of an applied magnetic field rotated in the b-c plane. We observe substantial oscillations in the thermal conductivity as a function of field angle, and, utilizing the experimentally determined Fermi surface, we model this phenomenon for all potential gap structures in UTe 2 . This allows us to identify point nodes near the b-axis, implying that the superconducting order parameter most likely belongs to the B 2 u irreducible representation of the crystal point group.

articles.title:
Mapping Aluminum
Flows in the United States Using
Advanced Bayesian Material Flow Analysis
articles.abstract: Abstract This paper presents a Bayesian material flow analysis (MFA) of aluminum in the U.S. economy, reconciling a 2017 baseline and updating the system through 2022. We introduce ARCADE (Abiotic Resource Cycles, Allocations, and Dynamics in the Economy), a unified Bayesian MFA framework integrating system definition, data pedigree, and probabilistic reconciliation under physical constraints. ARCADE combines government statistics, trade records, and industry reports into a physically consistent network and reports uncertainty-aware metrics. Results show continued U.S. reliance on imports of unwrought and finished aluminum products. The posterior median end-of-life (EOL) collection rate was 66.8% [57.2%, 79.9%] in 2017 and 67.6% [62.3%, 73.9%] in 2022. Median domestic retention of collected EOL scrap was lower in 2022 (52.7% [49.6%, 55.6%]) than in 2017 (56.4% [51.7%, 60.5%]), although the credible interval for the change spanned zero. Across robustness cases varying source weighting, pedigree-to-uncertainty mappings, and prior strength, domestic retention remained below 60%. Spatial analysis identified mismatches between EOL scrap generation and domestic remelting capacity. These findings show that improved collection alone may not increase domestic recycling when processing constraints persist. We observe a continued import dependence, efficient circulation of prompt fabrication scrap, and limited domestic retention of collected EOL scrap.

articles.title:
Unresolved Complex
Mixture of Hydrocarbons as a Potential
Stratigraphic Anthropogenic Marker for the Great Acceleration
articles.abstract: Abstract The unresolved complex mixture (UCM) consists of chromatographically unresolvable branched, cyclic, and aromatic hydrocarbons, which are intermediate- to semivolatile organic compounds primarily derived from anthropogenic fossil fuel usage, including industrial emissions and gasoline and diesel exhaust. The UCM in natural archives, expressed as its ratio to resolved compounds (UCM/R), may thus provide an indication of fossil fuel-derived contamination in the environment over time. To test this hypothesis, accurately dated sediment records from the Black Sea, the Baltic Sea, and the northeastern Germany Tiefer See lake were analyzed for hydrocarbons. Each record presents a similar temporal pattern with a synchronous main increase of UCM/R in the early 1950s and a decrease in the 1990s. This UCM/R pattern most likely reflects the pronounced increase in the use of petroleum-derived products during the Great Acceleration of the mid-20th century and, subsequently, the application of filters and catalytic converters to reduce volatile organic compound emissions in the 1980s–1990s. Therefore, UCM/R in recent sediments represents a stratigraphic anthropogenic marker for the Great Acceleration in European midlatitudes and, if replicated globally, could be a further marker for the beginning of the Anthropocene as a potential geological epoch.

articles.title: A hierarchical metabolic flux orchestrates cell cycle transitions in bacteria

Identification
and
Reaction Analysis of Antibiotic
Transformation Products in an Urban River via Suspect and Nontarget
Screening with a Self-Curated Library
articles.abstract: Abstract Antibiotics enter urban river basins mainly through sewage effluent. They undergo transformation during treatment and in river systems, generating transformation products (TPs) that may still have ecological effects. Yet, identifying these TPs by high-resolution mass spectrometry is hindered by the scarcity of reference standards and comprehensive MS/MS spectral libraries. To overcome this, we constructed a dedicated MS/MS library containing over 6,500 MS/MS spectra for 244 parent antibiotics and 362 TPs, thereby enabling rapid suspect screening through spectral matching. For novel TPs beyond library coverage, we integrated diagnostic fragment searching and seed-driven molecular networking to propagate annotations to structurally related unknowns. Applying this workflow to water, sediment, and effluent samples from an urban river system in Beijing, we identified 39 parent antibiotics and 158 TPs, of which 20 TPs are not previously documented in environmental samples. The major transformation reactions were cleavage, dealkylation, and hydrolysis, alongside compound-specific pathways like hemiacetal formation for erythromycin. These reactions differentially affect the environmental properties of antibiotics, and some reactions (e.g., dehydrogenation and dehydration) showed potential to enhance ecotoxicity. These results confirm that transformation substantially diversifies antibiotic signatures in urban aquatic environments and underscore the necessity of including TPs in environmental monitoring and risk assessment.

articles.title:
Microplastics
Promote
Light-Driven Ferrihydrite Transformation
by Altering the Balance between Interfacial Aggregation and Redox
Processes
articles.abstract: Abstract Ferrihydrite (Fh) phototransformation regulates iron cycling and the mobility of nutrients and contaminants in aquatic and terrestrial environments. Microplastics (MPs) increasingly coexist with Fh, yet whether intact MP particles regulate Fh phototransformation through particle-scale interfacial effects remains unclear. We investigated how MPs (polystyrene (PS), polyvinyl chloride (PVC), and polylactic acid (PLA)) affect Fh transformation under simulated solar irradiation. Without MPs, irradiation produced predominantly hematite (Hm), with goethite (Gt) as a minor product, and 9.17% of Fh was transformed after 25 d. MPs increased the transformation without changing detectable products. MPs suppressed Fh reaggregation by shifting surface charge and disrupting Fh–Fh contacts, while enhancing irradiation-induced charge separation, surface Fe(III) reduction, Fe(III)/Fe(II) cycling, and Fe mobilization. The promoting effects outweighed aggregation inhibition, causing net promotion of Fh transformation. Notably, PLA hydrolysis and photo-oxidation lowered pH and released acidic, Fe-complexing photoproducts, amplifying Fe mobilization and the aqueous Fe pathway. Overall, the PLA > PVC > PS trend reflects coupled polymer chemistry, particle properties, intact-particle interactions, and irradiation susceptibility, with PLA-derived aqueous components providing an additional solution-phase contribution. These findings show that intact MPs and polymer-derived aqueous products jointly modify Fe mineral evolution, linking plastic aging to iron biogeochemistry in illuminated surface environments.

articles.title:
Ultrafast
NH4+ Capture by Prussian
Blue Analogues Accelerated by the Hydrogen-Bond of Water
articles.abstract: Abstract Recovering ammonium (NH4+) from low-concentration wastewater represents a critical step toward sustainable nitrogen management. Although adsorption is widely regarded as the most promising strategy for NH4+ recovery from dilute streams, its practical application is often hampered by intrinsically slow kinetics and insufficient selectivity. Given the exceptional ion-sieving capability of Prussian blue analogues (PBAs), we hypothesized that water molecules confined within their framework channels create a dynamic hydrogen-bonded microenvironment that can modulate NH4+ transport. Inspired by this concept, we synthesized a series of Zn-based PBAs with controlled water contents via thermal treatment (denoted as Zn-PBAs-x, where x represents the treatment temperature). The sample with the highest water content (Zn-PBAs-60) exhibited an unprecedented NH4+ adsorption rate, with a pseudo-second-order rate constant (k2) of 4.35 g·mg–1·min–1. Integrated solid-state 1H magic-angle-spinning nuclear magnetic resonance (1H MAS NMR) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed a “water-accelerated adsorption” mechanism: hydrogen-bonding interactions between framework nitrogen sites and water molecules significantly weaken the binding of NH4+ to the framework, thereby markedly accelerating NH4+ migration within the channels. This material achieved nearly 20-fold concentration of dilute NH4Cl within 3 min. This study provides new insights and strategic directions for the rapid enrichment and resource utilization of low-concentration ammonia nitrogen, contributing to the advancement of sustainable development pathways.

articles.title:
Dissolved
Organic Matter Charge Dynamics over Three
Decades
articles.abstract: Abstract Dissolved organic matter (DOM) is a crucial component of aquatic ecosystems, influencing pH, metal speciation, and the bioavailability of trace elements. The influence of DOM on water quality depends not only on its concentration but also on its chemical characteristics. To quantify the site density (SD) of organic acid functional groups, a key characteristic of DOM, this study utilized data from over 31,000 water samples collected from 110 watercourses between 1995 and 2024 by Swedish national monitoring programs. We found systematic dynamic trends in SD across Sweden. The analysis revealed an increase in SD from 1995 to 2003, followed by a decline from 2003 to 2010. Since 2010, SD has stabilized, although modest increases remain evident at many sites. Earlier trends were potentially governed by changes in DOM mobility associated with recovery from acid deposition, whereas more recent trends are likely linked to DOM source characteristics.

articles.title:
A Substitution Paradox
in China’s Plastics
Sector: Climate Benefits of Degradable Materials Are Conditional on
Energy-System Decarbonization
articles.abstract: Abstract Plastics are a rapidly growing source of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Degradable plastics are increasingly promoted to address plastic waste concerns, while biobased alternatives are also considered for their potential to reduce reliance on fossil feedstocks and lower life cycle GHG emissions. However, their system-level climate effects remain uncertain because existing assessments often focus on individual products or polymers and rarely account for realistic substitution feasibility, value-chain interactions, and end-of-life (EoL) constraints. Here, we integrated dynamic material flow analysis, life cycle assessment, and scenario modeling to evaluate the net GHG implications of substituting degradable plastics across China’s plastics sector. The framework tracks five major conventional resins across 14 application sectors, links sector-specific substitution pathways with production-stage carbon intensities, and quantifies emission trajectories from 2025 to 2030, with long-term mitigation pathways explored to 2060. Technically feasible substitution increases cumulative life cycle GHG emissions by 7.1% relative to the conventional baseline because higher upstream production emissions outweigh potential EoL credits for recovered energy or displaced coproducts. Scenario analysis identifies a critical transition threshold: degradable plastics achieve net GHG reductions only when energy-system carbon intensity decreases by approximately 47% of the baseline level. The climate benefits of substitution are therefore conditional on coordinated energy-system decarbonization, production improvement, and waste-management development. Even under the optimistic pathway, 0.24 Gt CO2e of residual emissions remain in 2060, indicating the need for complementary mitigation measures.

articles.title:
Integrated Network
Toxicology and Multi-Level Validations
Unravel the Potential Mechanism Linking Phthalate Ester Exposure and
Endocrine Diseases
articles.abstract: Abstract Phthalate esters (PAEs) are endocrine-disrupting chemicals that can imitate endogenous hormones to disrupt the endocrine system. However, the upstream molecular initiating events (MIEs) by which PAEs trigger endocrine diseases, especially their interactions with receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs), remain poorly understood. Here, we discovered that the targets of low molecular weight (LMW) and high molecular weight (HMW) PAEs highly overlapped with breast cancer-related targets, with an even greater overlap for HMW PAEs. Mechanistically, PAEs promoted breast cancer progression by activating the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mediated signaling pathway, with EGFR identified as a key kinase. Molecular interaction analysis confirmed that PAEs directly bind to EGFR, inducing its dimerization, with the benzene ring, ketone, methyl, and ether groups of PAEs being crucial. Notably, HMW PAEs exhibited stronger dimerization effects. This PAE-induced EGFR dimerization was determined to be the MIE in PAE-induced breast cancer. Furthermore, PAEs increased EGFR expression (2.44-fold), subsequently activating the PI3K-Akt signaling pathway, which promoted breast cancer cell proliferation to 165.34% and tumor growth to 229.05% of the control, with HMW PAEs again having stronger effects. This study identifies a previously unrecognized MIE–PAE-induced EGFR dimerization, linking PAE exposure to RTK–driven breast cancer and offering potential targets for prevention and intervention in breast cancer.

articles.title:
Plankton
Size Structure Impacts PAH Bioaccumulation
and Fate in Marine Pelagic Food Webs
articles.abstract: Abstract Plankton constitutes the primary entry point of contaminants into pelagic food webs, yet the role of plankton size structure in governing hydrocarbon fate remains poorly understood due to methodological limitations. Here, polycyclic aromatic (PAHs) and aliphatic (AHs) hydrocarbons were investigated across seven plankton size fractions (0.7 μm to >500 μm) collected in coastal waters of the northwestern Mediterranean Sea using a locally designed online sequential filtration system. Biochemical, isotopic, and molecular marker analyses were combined to characterize plankton composition, hydrocarbon sources, and PAH bioaccumulation patterns across size fractions. Molecular markers confirmed the transition from phytoplankton-dominated signatures in the smallest fractions to increasing zooplanktonic contributions in larger fractions. The 0.7–2.7 and 2.7–20 μm fractions, dominated by pico- and nanoplankton, accounted for the highest particulate organic carbon and hydrocarbon concentrations (3.0–3.4 μg g–1 dw for Σ26-PAHs) while zooplankton fractions (>60 μm) displayed lower values (0.09–0.69 μg g–1 dw). The passive uptake of low-molecular-weight (LMW) PAHs dominated across all size fractions but decreased with increasing plankton size. In contrast, high-molecular-weight (HMW) PAHs showed preferential accumulation in nanoplankton. These results demonstrate that plankton size structure and biomass dependent processes strongly influence PAH bioaccumulation and trophic transfer in marine pelagic food webs.

articles.title:
Decoupling Ion Selectivity
and Transport via Dual-Scale
Interlayer Nanochannels in Reduced Graphene Oxide Membranes for Lithium
Separation
articles.abstract: Abstract Selective separation of Li+ from coexisting Ni2+, Co2+, and Mn2+ is an important step in lithium recovery from spent lithium-ion batteries. Reduced graphene oxide (rGO) membranes offer a promising platform for this separation through their ångström-scale interlayer nanochannels. However, the same narrow nanochannels hinder ion diffusion, inducing a severe permeability–selectivity trade-off. To decouple ion selectivity from transport, we report a nanoconfined sol–gel strategy for constructing a dual-scale interlayer architecture in rGO membranes. Intercalated between graphene oxide layers, aluminosilicate (AS) sols serve as cross-linkers and in situ vapor sources. During thermal aging, sol–gel condensation generates vapor that expands un-cross-linked galleries into transport highways, while cross-linked domains retain ion-selective confinement. The architecture is tunable across ion-selective interlayer spacing (dS, 7.1–8.3 Å) and expanded interlayer spacing (dE, 34–94 Å). Compared with conventional rGO membranes, the optimized dual-scale spacing membrane increases Li+ permeability 5.4-fold in mixed-ion solution while achieving high divalent-ion selectivity (Li+/Ni2+ = 246, Li+/Co2+ = 391, Li+/Mn2+ = 448). Molecular dynamics simulations attribute this selectivity to asymmetric energy barriers imposed on Li+ and divalent cations within the cross-linked spacing, while the expanded spacing facilitates low-resistance transport. This work shows how nanoconfined sol–gel chemistry can open a design space for fabricating high-performance ion recovery membranes.

articles.title:
Function of Submerged
Macrophytes in the Distribution
of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Alternatives in Constructed
Wetlands: Role of Extracellular Polymeric Substances (EPS) in the
Phyllosphere
articles.abstract: Abstract Submerged macrophytes in constructed wetlands (CWs) are key to removing PFAS alternatives, which pose serious risks to aquatic ecosystems. Although phyllosphere extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) are crucial for contaminant uptake by submerged macrophytes, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we show that typical PFAS alternatives, 6:2 chlorinated polyfluoroalkyl ether sulfonate (F-53B) and hexafluoropropylene oxide dimer acid (GenX), accumulated in Vallisneria spinulosa (V. spinulosa) reached 17.49 ± 1.02 and 5.25 ± 0.36 μg/g DW, respectively, approximately 2.70 and 3.16-fold higher than those in Ceratophyllum demersum (C. demersum). Correspondingly, the phyllosphere EPS of V. spinulosa exhibited high accumulation of GenX and F-53B, with concentrations of 124.98 ± 4.70 and 99.53 ± 13.12 μg/g DW, respectively. Crucially, EPS binding with PFAS alternatives increased the hydrophilicity and induced structural reorganization, facilitating contaminant internalization into plant tissues. Meanwhile, metagenomic analysis revealed that the phyllosphere microenvironment selectively enriched microbial functional genes involved in antioxidant defense and EPS biosynthesis, thus supporting sustained contaminant capture in the phyllosphere interface. These findings reveal EPS-mediated mechanisms underlying PFAS alternative uptake by submerged macrophytes in CWs.

articles.title:
Paleoclimatic
Legacies
Help Explain Microbial Carbon
Use Efficiency in Thawing Permafrost
articles.abstract: Abstract Microbial decomposition in thawing permafrost mobilizes one of Earth’s largest organic carbon reservoirs, releasing CO2 that amplifies global warming. This carbon–climate feedback depends strongly on microbial carbon use efficiency (CUE)─the ratio of biomass carbon synthesis to total carbon uptake, which governs the balance between carbon retention and respiratory loss. Although permafrost carbon and microbial communities developed thousands of years ago, how paleoclimatic legacies shape permafrost CUE remains unresolved. Here, by integrating 18O–H2O labeling with amplicon and metagenomic sequencing across a ∼1000-km transect on the Tibetan Plateau, we show that mid-Holocene paleoclimate outperforms contemporary drivers in explaining spatial variation in permafrost CUE. Sites with drier and more variable paleoclimates exhibited lower CUE (0.17 ± 0.07) than wetter and more climatically stable sites (0.43 ± 0.08). This lower CUE was linked to two pathways: geochemical constraints involving reduced nutrient availability and stronger phosphorus limitation, and microbial adaptations reflected in communities enriched in metabolically costly stress-tolerance and recalcitrant carbon-acquisition traits. Collectively, these paleoclimatic legacies accounted for 70% of CUE variation, underscoring the critical role of paleoclimate in shaping the vulnerability of permafrost carbon to respiratory loss upon thawing. Incorporating these millennial-scale legacies into Earth system models could improve projections of future permafrost carbon feedbacks.

articles.title:
Rapid
Emission–Economy Decoupling alongside
the Urbanization of Chinese Counties
articles.abstract: Abstract As China makes progress in air pollution control, the growing need for targeted pollution mitigation poses a great challenge for fine-scale emission tracking. However, the lack of up-to-date high-resolution emission data precludes a timely, spatially detailed assessment of emission distributions and their evolution with economic development. Here we derive summertime nitrogen oxides emissions from 2018 to 2024 for a total of 2,842 counties at different levels of urbanization in mainland China, based on satellite measurements and a fast, physics-based emission inversion method. The results show widespread declines in 84.1 ± 7.3% of counties. Among the 1,779 counties with available gross domestic product data, 76.7 ± 7.1% achieve absolute emission-economy decoupling (i.e., reduced emissions despite economic growth), and an additional 9.4 ± 3.9% exhibit relative decoupling (i.e., economic growth outpacing emissions growth). Relative emission reductions and emission-economy decoupling tend to be stronger in more urbanized counties, with the share of total national emissions moving toward less-urbanized, previously less-focused counties, particularly in the west. These results suggest structural progress toward greener development in Chinese counties along with an emerging need to shift attention toward less-urbanized locations.

articles.title:
Impacts of Biological
Filtration on Disinfection Byproduct
Control during Drinking Water Purification: A Critical Review
articles.abstract: Abstract Biofiltration, particularly biological activated carbon and sand filtration, is widely implemented as a low-chemical, energy-efficient barrier to attenuate disinfection byproduct (DBP) precursors. However, biofilters are living, time-evolving ecosystems that can transition from a net “sink” to a net “source” of reactive precursors. This review synthesized evidence that biofiltration exhibits selective removal: hydrophobic and high-molecular-weight C-DBP precursors are preferentially removed, whereas hydrophilic N-DBP (e.g., HANs, NDMA) precursors readily break through and may be newly produced. The authors clarified the mechanistic basis of precursor generation, highlighting (i) biofilm turnover that releases intracellular organic matter enriched in amines and nucleic acids, (ii) continuous production and sloughing of soluble microbial products and extracellular polymeric substances that elevate protein-like DON, and (iii) media aging and stratification that diminish removal efficacy. Regression analysis estimated sink–source transition for N-DBP precursor removal at approximately log10(bed volumes) = 5.38 (∼240,000 bed volumes), a practical reference in drinking water treatment plants. Furthermore, the authors identified critical operational tipping points, including oxidant pre-exposure, temperature fluctuations, and nutrient stoichiometry, that can trigger this functional inversion. Finally, a risk-oriented framework is proposed, advocating for precursor-specific monitoring (e.g., fluorescence signatures) and intelligent process control to stabilize biofilter performance against emerging genotoxic risks.

articles.title:
Evaluating Pollution
Prevention Effectiveness for
Toxic Substances in Canada Using Advanced Difference-in-Differences
Methods
articles.abstract: Abstract This study evaluates the effectiveness of pollution prevention (P2) activities using facility-level data from Canada’s National Pollutant Release Inventory (NPRI) over 1993–2024. Leveraging recent advances in causal inference methodology that account for staggered treatment adoption and heterogeneous treatment effects, this Difference-in-Differences (DiD) analysis moves beyond conventional DiD to identify substantial heterogeneity in P2 impacts across time, sectors, regions, P2 activities, and substances. Key findings indicate analysis of staggered adoption matters, with cohort-specific release reductions ranging widely, and larger effects among earlier adoption cohorts (2001–2003 ∼0-76 vs 2021 ∼3%). P2 adoption is associated with an average 19% reduction in pollutant releases. In contrast, P2 activities are associated with a near-zero and statistically insignificant increase in waste. P2 is more effective for releases to water, and within specific sectors such as Mining and Quarrying and Conventional Oil and Gas extraction. Stronger effects are observed for activities related to Inventory Management/Purchasing, and in Ontario, Alberta, and Quebec, and for VOCs. Despite study limitations, the results suggest that P2 delivers net environmental benefits overall and highlight the importance of modern causal inference methods for evaluating P2 policies in settings with staggered treatment adoption, such as the NPRI.

articles.title:
Unignorable Role
of Iron Redox and Microbial Adaptation
in Mediating Arsenic-Induced Suppression of Carbon Emissions in Paddy
Soils
articles.abstract: Abstract Arsenic (As) contamination disturbs organic carbon (OC) cycling in paddy soils, potentially influenced by microbial adaptive evolution and redox-active iron (Fe). Here, the association of As with C emissions (CH4 and CO2), microbes, and Fe dynamics in flooded paddy soils was investigated via microcosm experiments across two As levels (20 and 200 mg kg–1). Results showed that As contamination markedly inhibited CH4 (>90%) and CO2 (>38%) emissions, accompanied by inhibited ferric reduction, decreased OC bioavailability, and shifted microbial communities toward As-tolerant and oligotrophic strategies. Correlation analysis and validation experiments demonstrated that Fe reduction covaried negatively with available As but positively with C bioavailability indicators (p < 0.001). The suppressed C emissions under low-dose As were closely linked to perturbed Fe redox cycling, while high-dose As appeared to amplify this inhibition through additional microbial toxicity and community restructuring. Exogenous zerovalent iron increased CH4 emissions by 0.92–19.54-fold through coupled changes in As immobilization, redox conditions, C bioavailability, and abundance of Fe-reducing bacteria and methanogens. This work indicated that Fe redox and microbial adaptation are important contributors to As-mediated suppression of C emissions, providing evidence for the As–Fe–C nexus and offering insights for balancing As remediation with C emission mitigation.

articles.title:
Turning
Abandoned
Mines into Carbon Sinks: Laboratory
Demonstration of CO2 Hydrate Sequestration in Cold-Region
Goafs under Permafrost Conditions
articles.abstract: Abstract Carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) is a key technology for carbon neutrality, but conventional CO2 geological sequestration suffers from high injection pressure, limited stability, and restricted storage space. Hydrate-based CO2 sequestration offers high capacity, low cost, and intrinsic safety. This study proposes a novel in situ CO2 hydrate formation and sequestration method in coal mine goafs containing permafrost layers in cold regions. The natural low-temperature permafrost environment provides favorable conditions for hydrate formation, while goafs offer large storage space. To avoid hydrate plugging and improve engineering feasibility, a liquid-first CO2 constant-pressure supply and predissolution mode was adopted. We simulated goaf conditions at depths of 110–130 m and ∼1 MPa. Experiments tested three injection temperatures (293.15, 298.15, and 303.15 K) and five goaf temperatures (269.15–277.15 K) using tetrahydrofuran and tryptophan as promoters. Results proved efficient sequestration at a low pressure of 1 MPa. Under optimal conditions (injection temperature of 298.15 K, goaf temperature of 271.15 K), capacity reached 60.9 mmol of CO2/mol of water (mmol/mol) with an efficiency of 135.36 (kg·m–3)/MPa. The 26.7 h stability experiments under depressurization showed 4.21–16.09 mmol/mol dissociated initially, but 66.38%–90.77% CO2 remained sequestered. Further, one-month tests under the pressure-release condition revealed hydrate dissociation almost stopped after day 1, yielding a 65.32% permanent sequestration ratio. Crucially, under the pressure-maintained condition, the system continued to form CO2 hydrates over the 30-day period, resulting in an additional 31.04% CO2 storage. These results validate the feasibility and long-term stability of this novel approach.

articles.title:
Strategies for Eliminating
Heavy Air Pollution in
the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei Region: Insights from Joint
Practices during the 2022 Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games
articles.abstract: Abstract The 2022 Olympic Winter Games (OWG) and Paralympic Winter Games (PWG) marked the first time the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei (BTH) region implemented joint air pollution prevention and control measures for a winter mega-event. Notably, while Beijing maintained clean air (daily PM2.5 concentration ≤ 75 μg/m3, according to the Ambient Air Quality Standards in effect at the time) during the OWG, a heavy-pollution episode occurred during the PWG, with the 24-h average PM2.5 concentration peaking at 155 μg/m3. Combining field observations, dynamic emission characterization, and The Comprehensive Air quality Model with extensions (CAMx) simulations, we conducted a closed-loop study to investigate the underlying causes of this episode. Results show that while the industrial sector effectively regulated emissions, the mobile-source activity levels recovered rapidly after the Chinese New Year, outweighing the control measures implemented for mobile sources. This recovery increased total NOx emissions by 13% in the BTH region, driving nitrate-dominated PM2.5 pollution. During the study period, the PM2.5 nitrate concentration (normalized by the carbon monoxide concentration) was found to increase by 3 × 10–4 and 1 × 10–5 for each one-ton increase in NOx emissions in Beijing and the BTH region, respectively. To eliminate heavy PM2.5 pollution under the meteorological conditions observed during the PWG, NOx emissions would need to be further reduced by ≥1% in Beijing and ≥7% in the BTH region. This work underscores the urgent need to mitigate emissions from diesel trucks and nonroad machinery, especially under extremely adverse meteorological conditions in the BTH region.

articles.title:
Gradient-Charge
Oxygen Vacancy Pairs Enable Synergistic
Activation of O2 and H2O for Low-Temperature
CH3CN Emission Control
articles.abstract: Abstract Acetonitrile (CH3CN) emitted from industrial production severely threatens atmospheric quality due to its persistence and high toxicity. While selective catalytic oxidation (SCO) represents the most promising technology for CH3CN elimination, the inherent competition between O2-activated oxidation and H2O-activated hydrolysis pathways has long prevented the simultaneous achievement of excellent low-temperature activity and high N2 selectivity. Herein, we report a Cu-modified TiO2 catalyst and propose a Cu-induced gradient-charge oxygen vacancy pair structure (Ti–OVR–Cu–OVP–Ti) as the most plausible active site configuration that enables activation of O2 and H2O via electron filling of their antibonding orbitals to promote the reaction during CH3CN oxidation. The electron-rich OVR site can adsorb both O2 and H2O, donating electrons to populate the π* antibonding orbital of O2 and the σ* antibonding orbital of H2O. Meanwhile, the electron-poor OVP site adsorbs O2 or H2O and serves as a reservoir to sustain a continuous supply of active species. The optimized catalyst induced by Ti–OVR–Cu–OVP–Ti structure achieves complete CH3CN conversion at 220 °C with 96% N2 selectivity. This work highlights the critical role of electron configuration in tailoring oxygen vacancy functions, providing a general strategy for developing advanced environmental catalysts for practical CH3CN emission control.

articles.title:
A Scenario-Based
Probabilistic First-Tier Screening
of Potential Chemical Risk to European Groundwater Ecosystems
articles.abstract: Abstract Groundwater supplies much of the freshwater used by humans while supporting highly specialized biological communities characterized by high endemism and limited taxonomic, functional, and phylogenetic redundancy. Yet European Union groundwater legislation remains resource-oriented and addresses the ecological consequences of chemical contamination only indirectly. We conducted a continent-wide, first-tier screening of potential chemical risk to European groundwater ecosystems. Harmonized European surface water and groundwater monitoring data were combined with geostatistical interpolation and transport modeling to estimate contaminant concentrations at the groundwater table, while uncertainty in hydrogeological conditions, chemical fate, and preferential transport was propagated through Monte Carlo simulations. We compared a Surface Water Baseline scenario, based on model-derived groundwater concentrations and existing freshwater regulatory thresholds, with a Groundwater-Informed Conservative scenario integrating measured groundwater concentrations, groundwater-fauna toxicity data, and precautionary adjustments where groundwater-specific evidence was unavailable. Potential risk was summarized as the average frequency of exceedance (AFE) across contaminants and uncertainty realizations; its maps indicate the frequency and spatial distribution of threshold exceedances, not their magnitude or the severity of ecological damage. Mean AFE was low under the baseline scenario but increased 5-fold under the conservative scenario, revealing areas in the medium-to-very-high screening classes in the Pyrenean–Catalan sector, Sierra Nevada, and the eastern Balkan–Carpathian region. The framework provides a replicable basis for prioritizing monitoring, ecotoxicological testing, and management.
